definitions.explanation: The counter reading for two of something flat: sheets of paper, tickets, plates, photos, or garments.

examples.japanese: チケットを{二枚|にまい}ください。
{紙|かみ}が{二枚|にまい}{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Two sheets of paper are left.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}かったので、シャツを{二枚|にまい}{重|かさ}ねて{着|き}て{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: It was cold, so I layered two shirts and went out.

notes:
{二枚|にまい} is the reading for "two" with the counter {枚|まい}, used for thin, flat things.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {二枚|にまい}{重|かさ}ねる: to layer two of something
- {二枚|にまい}{組|ぐみ}: a two-disc or two-sheet set
- {二枚|にまい}おろし: filleting a fish into two pieces

RELATED EXPRESSION:
{二枚目|にまいめ} means "a good-looking man," from the second billboard in an Edo-period theater lineup. It is not simply "the second flat object."

RELATED COUNTERS:
- {一枚|いちまい}: one flat object
- {何枚|なんまい}: how many flat objects
